title: Por su parte: introducir un nuevo caso dentro de una comparación

sections.content: Por su parte (for its/his/her part) introduces a new subject within an ongoing comparison, signaling this one, in contrast or in addition to what came before -- useful when a reading moves from one country's experience to another's. It agrees with the subject it refers back to (mi parte, tu parte, su parte, etc., though su parte is by far the most common in historical writing). These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Uruguay, por su parte, vivió también un episodio poco frecuente entre las dictaduras de la región.
items.english: Uruguay, for its part, also experienced an episode uncommon among the region's dictatorships.

items.spanish: Los Tupamaros, por su parte, ya estaban prácticamente derrotados militarmente hacia 1972.
items.english: The Tupamaros, for their part, were already practically defeated militarily by 1972.

items.spanish: El régimen, por su parte, no esperaba que la ciudadanía rechazara la nueva constitución.
items.english: The regime, for its part, didn't expect the public to reject the new constitution.

items.spanish: Sanguinetti, por su parte, heredaría un país con una economía debilitada y profundas heridas sociales.
items.english: Sanguinetti, for his part, would inherit a country with a weakened economy and deep social wounds.

sections.content: Por su parte usually follows the subject it introduces, set off by commas -- it's a smoother alternative to starting every new sentence in a comparison with en cambio or sin embargo.
